item.text:
**3B.7 Research Note**

Bottom line: the 2024 record is overwhelmingly negative. Hasina’s government did not convincingly protect women, children, minorities, or other vulnerable groups from targeted violence or systematic neglect; the strongest evidence instead shows state-linked violence against protesters, attacks on minorities after the August collapse, and continued insecurity for Rohingya and host communities. The positive material is mostly humanitarian partner activity, not direct proof of effective protection by Hasina herself.

**Negative Evidence**
- [Bangladesh: Security Forces Target Unarmed Students](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/07/22/bangladesh-security-forces-target-unarmed-students) — Human Rights Watch, July 22, 2024. Summary: HRW reported army deployment, shutdowns, and security-force violence against student protesters, with attacks by Awami League-affiliated student activists as well; this is direct evidence against protecting vulnerable civilians from targeted violence. IDs: `3B.7`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`
- [Bangladesh: Prime Minister Hasina Resigns amid Mass Protests](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/06/bangladesh-prime-minister-hasina-resigns-amid-mass-protests) — Human Rights Watch, August 6, 2024. Summary: HRW says violence included security forces and Chhatra League attacks on protesters, plus reports of extrajudicial killings and enforced disappearances during the crackdown; that weighs heavily against protection of women, children, and other vulnerable people caught in the violence. IDs: `3B.7`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `2B.4`, `2B.9`
- [Vandalism, Attacks Follow Bangladesh Prime Minister’s Exit](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/08/vandalism-attacks-follow-bangladesh-prime-ministers-exit) — Human Rights Watch, August 8, 2024. Summary: After Hasina’s departure, HRW reported attacks on Hindus, Ahmadiyya Muslims, and ethnic minorities, including homes and temples being torched; this shows the state did not leave minorities protected against targeted reprisals in 2024. IDs: `3B.7`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `2B.4`
- [Bangladesh: Repression, Security Force Abuses Discredit Elections](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/bangladesh-repression-security-force-abuses-discredit-elections) — Human Rights Watch, January 11, 2024. Summary: HRW reported repression, arrests for criticism, and widespread security-force abuse before the January election; this is early-2024 evidence that the regime was already failing vulnerable political opponents and civil society. IDs: `3B.7`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`
- [Bangladesh’s crackdown on protesters left more than 170 dead, U.N. says](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights) — United Nations / OHCHR, July 26, 2024. Summary: The UN said more than 170 people had been killed and warned that internet shutdowns increase impunity; this strongly indicates the state response was not protective and instead created a fear and impunity environment affecting vulnerable people broadly. IDs: `3B.7`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `2B.4`, `2B.9`
- [Bangladesh: army enforces curfew as student-led protests spiral](https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-student-led-protests-spiral/2182818/) — Reuters, July 20, 2024. Summary: Reuters described internet/text shutdowns, curfew, and army deployment during the crackdown; that is evidence of coercive state action rather than protection of civilians from harm. IDs: `3B.7`, `3B.5`, `3B.6`, `3B.1`

**Limited Positive Evidence**
- [UN and partners seek $852.4m to support Rohingya refugees and Bangladeshi hosts](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/263209-un-and-partners-seek-8524m-support-rohingya-refugees-and-bangladeshi-hosts) — UNHCR / UN in Bangladesh, March 13, 2024. Summary: The 2024 Rohingya response plan was presented under Bangladeshi authorities and aimed to provide food, shelter, health care, protection, education, and livelihood support to women, children, and host communities; this is real protection infrastructure, but it is mostly partner-led and does not prove Hasina personally insulated vulnerable groups from violence. IDs: `3B.7`, `2B.3`
- [UNICEF and JAPAN join hands to improve the well-being of Bangladeshi and Rohingya children living in Bhasan Char Island and Cox’s Bazar](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/262180-unicef-and-japan-join-hands-improve-the-well-being-of-bangladeshi-and-rohingya-children-living) — United Nations in Bangladesh, March 3, 2024. Summary: UNICEF reported expanded services for Rohingya refugee children, women, and host communities in Cox’s Bazar and Bhasan Char, including education, WASH, health, and nutrition; this is positive for vulnerable-group protection, but again it reflects humanitarian delivery rather than a demonstrated protective political strategy by Hasina. IDs: `3B.7`
- [UNFPA Bangladesh Annual Report 2024](https://bangladesh.unfpa.org/en/unfpa-bangladesh-annual-report-2024) — UNFPA Bangladesh, 2024. Summary: The report describes large-scale GBV services, safe deliveries, menstrual supplies, and emergency assistance for women and girls, including Rohingya camps and disaster-affected districts; this shows some functioning protection services existed, but it does not establish that Hasina’s government reliably prevented targeted violence or systematic neglect. IDs: `3B.7`, `2B.4`
- [UNFPA and Japan sign $3.3 million assistance to Protect Rohingya Refugee and Host Community Women and girls in Cox's Bazar and Noakhali Districts](https://bangladesh.unfpa.org/en/news/unfpa-and-japan-sign-33-million-assistance-protect-rohingya-refugee-and-host-community-women) — UNFPA Bangladesh, October 22, 2024. Summary: This partnership targeted Rohingya refugee women and girls plus host communities for GBV prevention, SRHR, and safe spaces; it is a concrete protection measure, but it is external-partner driven and only weakly attributable to Hasina’s own protection performance. IDs: `3B.7`
- [Rising Together: Empowering Women and Youth to Build Resilient Refugee and Host Communities in Bangladesh](https://bangladesh.unfpa.org/en/news/rising-together-empowering-women-and-youth-build-resilient-refugee-and-host-communities) — UNFPA Bangladesh, December 3, 2024. Summary: UNFPA and Switzerland launched a program for Rohingya and host-community women and youth focused on GBV, SRHR, education, and mental health; this supports the existence of protection-oriented services, but not a strong finding that Hasina’s state itself effectively protected vulnerable groups. IDs: `3B.7`

**Search Gap**
- I did not find strong 2024 evidence that Hasina personally created or enforced a robust protection regime for minorities, women, children, or other vulnerable groups.
- The clearest direct evidence points the other way: state violence against protesters, attacks on minorities after the regime’s collapse, and ongoing insecurity for Rohingya.
- The best positive evidence is humanitarian service delivery by UN agencies and donors in Bangladesh, which is real but only weakly attributable to Hasina’s protective governance.
